description: On startup, seeds the working rules file from the shipped default unless it already exists. On every session start, and whenever the data-directory rules file changes, narrows agents/ to the fleet agents those rules let anyone reach, watches that file, and asks each session for /reload-plugins when its set changed; an invalid rules or models file leaves agents/ as it is, and a session with FLEET_RULES set leaves agents/ to the data-directory file. Before every Agent, Skill, Workflow and Bash call, identifies the caller: the main session's Agent calls are checked against the main section and its other calls pass; a fleet subagent's Agent calls are checked against its row in rules, its Skill and Bash calls against the disallowed lists, and its Workflow calls are refused; an Agent call to a fleet agent, from either, is refused unless the rules file mentions its model, and must pass one of the levels the rules give that model (any named level when they give none, no effort when they give only default; default beside named levels is a configuration error that refuses the call), and a missing, relative or unknown effort is refused; the fleet is the set of models the rules file mentions, one agent type per model, recognised by its definition or, when that file is gone, by its model id in the rules, and a type carrying the fleet prefix that neither resolves is refused; built-in subagents pass. A rules file that is not exactly one JSON object (an empty file, several documents, a top-level array or string, text that is not JSON; null reads as empty rules) makes these checks refuse. When a fleet agent starts, the same guard hands it the disallowed skills and commands, so it does not try them; a refused skill is not a reason to stop. Separately, an Agent call that targets a fleet agent is refused unless its prompt is a structured brief with the required sections; calls to other agent types are not inspected.
